title: LLM terrain scout and SLA risk calibrator
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description: Establish a repeatable scouting workflow and deliverables that map candidate open and commercial models against Redwood's SLA and latency-risk taxonomy. Produce a prioritized dossier for engineering and sales with actionable fallback and procurement triggers.
objectives: Create a standardized capability matrix covering latency, throughput, input-context behavior, quantization friendliness, and failure modes
Measure representative latency and cost under synthetic enterprise workloads across 6 candidate models and two hardware profiles
Define SLA risk bands and automated triggers for model fallbacks and routing policies
Deliver a field-ready dossier and a lightweight decision rubric for sales/solutions engineering
scope: Benchmarks: 3 sequence-length profiles (short, medium, long) and cold vs warm cache
Models: up to 6 candidates (mix of open and commercial) representative of likely customer fallbacks
Artifacts: model capability matrix, raw benchmark CSVs, a one-page dossier per model, and a decision rubric
out_of_scope: Deep model fine-tuning or prompting experiments beyond canonical prompts
Full legal/vendor contract review (procurement team will coordinate)
Longitudinal drift monitoring (future continuous signal project)
tasks: Kickoff: align stakeholders and agree acceptance criteria
Design synthetic workload profiles and canonical prompt set
Provision ephemeral infra and run baseline benchmarks
Qualitative probe: run adversarial prompts to catalog failure modes
Draft per-model dossier and decision rubric
Review with Eng (runtime) and Sales SEs, incorporate feedback
Finalize deliverables and handoff to Signals team for follow-up automation
acceptance_criteria: A capability matrix covering the specified metrics for all 6 models
Benchmarks reproducible from a public runbook and raw CSVs uploaded to the shared drive
A one-page dossier per model with clear SLA risk band and recommended fallback action
Decision rubric that maps customer latency tiers to specific model or routing policies
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime Eng and Head of Solutions Engineering
comments: 2026-03-10 Mateo Ruiz: Ticket created after cross-functional kickoff. Agreed 6 candidate models — list attached in runbook.

Trade-off: synthetic workloads intentionally under-index user diversity to keep repeats reproducible; will supplement with a small set of customer traces in a follow-up
Operational ask for Eng: expose per-model KV-cache hit rates in benchmark harness for better attribution
